# Pragmatism Lies Like a Corridor in a Hotel

As the young Italian pragmatist Papini has well said, pragmatism[^1] lies in the midst of our theories, like a corridor in a hotel.[^2] Innumerable chambers open out of it.[^3] In one you may find a man writing an atheistic volume; in the next someone on his knees praying for faith and strength; in a third a chemist investigating a body's properties.[^4] In a fourth a system of idealistic metaphysics is being excogitated; in a fifth the impossibility of metaphysics is being shown.[^5] But they all own the corridor, and all must pass through it if they want a practicable way of getting into or out of their respective rooms.[^6]
